clue.text: Had a disaster, trimming mushroom

indicators.note: trimming a word cuts a letter off its edge, here the final one

parts.note: blewits is a name for an edible lilac-stemmed mushroom
the last letter of the mushroom's name, cut off by the trim

explanation.surface: A cook ruined the dish while preparing a mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimming' removes the final S from BLEWITS, a mushroom also spelt without that S, which is why the surface feels like it defines itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone who bungled a chance completely is said to have done this.

clue.text: One going to take axe for execution

indicators.note: execution by beheading: the word loses its head, its first letter

parts.note: a cleaver is a heavy chopping blade, loosely an axe
the head letter of the chopping tool, struck off

explanation.surface: A condemned prisoner walks to the block where the axe waits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for execution' beheads CLEAVER, removing its first letter C; 'to take' simply joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym by description: a person departing, such as a pupil finishing school.

clue.text: Damage every article one puts on? You can't insure against that

definitions.text: Damage every article one puts on?
definitions.meaning: read whimsically as an instruction: put clothes on, then rip them
policies routinely exclude gradual deterioration from ordinary use

explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical reading of the phrase as putting on clothes and ripping them, plus the gradual deterioration that policies exclude.

clue.text: Went over meeting of two people to finalise Mary Poppins?

indicators.note: the two people meet, so their names stand side by side

parts.words: two people to finalise Mary Poppins
parts.note: P. L. Travers was the author of the Mary Poppins books

parts.words: two people to finalise Mary Poppins
parts.note: ED is short for editor, the other person who gets a book into its final form

explanation.surface: Someone reviewed a meeting where two people settled the final version of Mary Poppins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting of' joins the two people who would finish the book: its author P. L. Travers and her editor, abbreviated ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have crossed or passed across something.

clue.text: Caller from the mail after a devilish feature

parts.note: post is the Latin prefix meaning after, as in post-war
the devil is pictured with horns, so one of them is a feature of his

explanation.surface: A visitor arrives from the mail office following something fiendish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a position word but supplies letters itself. The mail here is the old mail coach, whose guard sounded this instrument to announce its arrival.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: the brass instrument blown by a mail-coach guard to announce the coach.

clue.text: I throw in jug

definitions.meaning: in baseball the player who delivers the ball to the batter
a large vessel with a handle and lip for pouring liquids

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the baseball player delivering the ball, and a large pouring vessel.

clue.text: Stop remarking on very short dress?

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: sh! is what you say to make someone stop talking
I FT, one foot, written as 1 ft: a very small length

explanation.surface: Someone is told to quit commenting on a tiny frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' stacks the pieces in this down entry. 'very short' is a measurement: 1 ft, written with I for the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a simple, loose, straight-cut woman's garment.

clue.text: In which athletes find something to pass round

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the two words that follow, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A relay race, where runners need a baton to hand on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals letters lying across 'which athletes'. The surface suggests a relay baton; the thing passed round is for collecting money.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: it is passed round a crowd to collect contributions.

clue.text: The thinking animal?

parts.note: a pun: to chew the cud and to ponder share one verb, so a cud-chewing beast is whimsically a thinker

explanation.definitionFit: Pun: cud-chewing beasts such as cows share their name with the verb for pondering deeply.

clue.text: Problem seeing pet carrying a little weight around

indicators.note: the pet holds the other piece inside itself

parts.note: a cat is a common household pet

indicators.note: around tells you the weight is turned to run backwards

parts.note: a carat is a tiny unit of weight, used for gemstones

explanation.surface: A portly animal is the trouble: its owner sees it has put on a few ounces round the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problem seeing pet' tempts you to look for a difficulty with an animal; the split falls after 'seeing'. 'around' gives TARAC, which 'carrying' tucks inside the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a clouding of the eye's lens that impairs vision.

clue.text: Eventually featured by news magazine

parts.note: something featured by a publication appears in it
Time is a well-known American weekly news magazine

explanation.surface: Someone finally gets a write-up in a weekly current-affairs publication.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sooner or later, after a while.

clue.text: Declining to scrap scripture period

indicators.note: to scrap something is to discard it, so the scripture letters are thrown out

parts.note: decadent means in a state of decline or decay
NT is the abbreviation for the New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to drop a religious studies lesson from the timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to scrap' removes NT from the end of DECADENT. 'Declining' reads as refusing but means decaying.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a span of ten years.

clue.text: Very unhappy about closing church that's coming to life

indicators.note: closing here means closing round, enclosing the church letters

parts.note: hating something is being very unhappy about it

explanation.surface: Parishioners are upset at the shutting of a church that had begun to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closing' reads as shutting the church down, but here it means closing round it: the word for 'very unhappy about' encloses the church's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: what a chick does as it emerges from its egg.

clue.text: Stolen wife or other felony put right

indicators.note: putting the letters right means setting them in their proper order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A list of crimes to be remedied: an abducted spouse, or some different offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put right' rearranges OTHER FELONY. She was wife of Menelaus of Sparta, carried off by Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Mythological description: the queen of Sparta abducted by Paris, starting a ten-year war.

clue.text: Leave great Britain say for somewhere tropical

parts.note: to desert is to leave or abandon
Great Britain is an example of an island

explanation.surface: A Briton quits the country for a place in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the palm-fringed castaway's refuge of popular imagination.

clue.text: Product of the sea becomes ready to drink?

parts.note: what something becomes is what it then is
a drink that ... has been poured and is ready to be drunk

explanation.surface: Something harvested from the ocean is turned into a beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces read as a phrase: a drink that 'is in glass' is poured and ready. The substance is a gelatin from fish bladders, used to clarify beer and wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a gelatin obtained from fish swim bladders.

clue.text: As conductor is, hearing principal of cellos going wrong

indicators.note: letters that go wrong fall out of their proper order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the principal is the leading one, so the leading letter of the next word

explanation.surface: The maestro listens as the lead cellist makes a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principal of' takes C from cellos, and 'going wrong' rearranges HEARING with that C.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a conductor directs the orchestra and has command of it.

clue.text: Riot: incident that could lead to ban

indicators.note: the letters could lead to a new word once rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A violent disturbance is the kind of episode that gets gatherings prohibited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that could lead to' rearranges RIOT INCIDENT; the definition is the single last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal prohibition, especially by a court or church.

clue.text: Restrictions in place to bar one song

indicators.note: to bar something is to exclude it, so the letter for one is shut out

parts.note: chains restrict whoever wears them
I is the Roman numeral for one
something that is on is in place, like a lid

explanation.surface: Rules have been introduced to prohibit a particular tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bar' removes the I from CHAINS ON. 'bar' also winks at the musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the French word for one, used in English for French cabaret numbers.

clue.text: One that shines as member of large Kent family?

parts.note: Kent is a county in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
a quin is one of quintuplets, five siblings born together: a member of a large family

explanation.surface: A star pupil, as you'd expect from a big clan in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read whimsically as a quin from the south-east: Kent is a county in England's SE corner, and a quin is one of five born together.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: a small sparkling disc sewn onto clothing.

clue.text: Appeal of article on timeless reform movement

indicators.note: in an across entry a piece placed on another is added after it
timeless means without time, so the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: Chartism was a 19th-century British working-class movement for political reform
T is the abbreviation for time
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about an enduring campaign for change proves attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' removes T from CHARTISM, the Victorian British campaign for voting reform, and 'on' adds A at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: personal magnetism that draws others.

clue.text: Singular speech? Not half

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: only half of the word for speech is kept, the opening four letters

parts.note: language is another word for speech

explanation.surface: Is that an odd way of talking? Absolutely!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps the first half of LANGUAGE after S. The whole clue also defines: 'not half' is itself a British colloquial phrase meaning 'very much so', an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: informal, peculiar talk, of which 'not half' (British for 'very much so') is itself a specimen.

clue.text: Good present, an ornamental frill

parts.note: to present something is to offer it

explanation.surface: A decorative ruffle makes a nice gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' reads as a gift but is the verb, to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary sense: a pleat or flute crimped into lace or fabric as decoration.

clue.text: In fashion house see foreign paper

indicators.note: the letter for see goes inside the fashion house's name

parts.note: Prada is an Italian luxury fashion house
V is short for vide, Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: At a couture label's office, someone spots an overseas newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' places V inside PRADA. V abbreviates the Latin 'vide', meaning see.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Russian daily, once the Soviet Communist Party's official newspaper.

clue.text: Surgeon's brief ban

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a veto is a ban or prohibition
the final letter of the word for ban, cut off

explanation.surface: A doctor is given a short suspension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts the final O from VETO. In Britain an animal doctor is formally a veterinary surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Short form: British animal doctors are formally called veterinary surgeons.

clue.text: Base defeat for swimmer

parts.note: a seat is a base, as in the seat of government
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A competitor in the pool suffers a shameful loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' reads as an adjective meaning shameful but is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a migratory fish, which crosswords call anything that swims.

clue.text: Writer got a new name in regular form

parts.note: a pen is a thing that writes

indicators.note: new tells you the two words before it are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An author adopted a pseudonym, filling in the standard paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regular form' suggests a standard document, yet it is a shape with equal sides. 'new' gives TAGO, and 'name' is not the new thing but a separate abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a five-sided figure, regular when its sides and angles are equal.

clue.text: Proverb influencing wife to leave

indicators.note: the wife's letter is to leave the word, so it is taken out

parts.note: swaying someone is influencing them
W is the genealogy abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: An old adage persuades a married woman to walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes W from SWAYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an adage or maxim.
